channel.name: RedHat Engineer

handles.note: Posting is done by hand by the operator from the Content Lab dashboard (RedHat Engineer section).

autonomy.authorized_by: operator, 2026-09-30, explicit instruction to convert this pipeline to the RedHat Engineer tech channel (previously authorized 2026-09-27 to run end to end without human approval)
autonomy.scope: Producing and uploading one video per run to Content Lab via scripts/run_episode.py. Does NOT authorize skipping compliance-and-safety.md boundaries.
autonomy.known_risk: No automated visual QA step exists for generated scenes -- see SKILL.md's 'Known accepted risk' note.

channel.publish_window: not yet scheduled -- workflow_dispatch only until the operator adds an on: schedule: block
channel.topic: The story and mysteries behind technological innovation, past and present: legends, disputed claims, missing papers and conspiracy theories told fairly, then checked against the record.

voice.model: edge-tts (Microsoft Edge online neural TTS, free, no API key, no quota)
voice.voice_note: Kept as the female narrator on 2026-09-30 when the pipeline was converted to the RedHat Engineer channel (the original RedHat pipeline used en-US-AndrewMultilingualNeural; the operator chose to keep the female voice). Log any further change in reports/changelog.md.

settings.audio_profile: Warm adult female narrator, confident and measured. Emotion is NOT via SSML/mstts:express-as (Microsoft blocks custom SSML server-side). Instead rate/volume/pitch are varied per script section to shape the arc of a technology story; see section_presets.

cold_open.note: The hook: the question or contradiction that makes someone stay. Slow and deliberate.

setup.note: Who, where, when, and what problem existed before the invention. Matter-of-fact.

rising_mystery.note: The bulk: the attempts, rivalries, failures and disputed claims. Faster and more energetic.

climax_reveal.note: The turn: what the record actually shows versus the legend. Slightly slower, more weight.

aftermath.note: Landing: what it means now, and what nobody can answer yet. Calm and quiet.

voice.chunking_rule: Generate narration 2-3 sentences at a time (looser than a Shorts channel's 1-2, proportionate to a 5-7 minute format). Save as chunk_0001.mp3, chunk_0002.mp3, ... in the episode's 03_audio/ folder, then stitch with scripts/stitch_audio.py.
voice.generation_notes: Generated locally with scripts/generate_narration_chunks.py (edge-tts Python package). Maps each chunk to its script.md section ([COLD_OPEN]/[SETUP]/[RISING_MYSTERY]/[CLIMAX_REVEAL]/[AFTERMATH]) to pick the right rate/volume/pitch preset.
voice.notes: Never change mid-video. Log any change with a dated reason in reports/changelog.md.

style_lock.image_prompt_suffix: hand-drawn black marker stickman on a clean white whiteboard, thick confident marker strokes, solid red marker fedora with black band, the stickman has exactly two black dot eyes and NO mouth, a neutral calm face, thin single-line stick limbs and a plain stick body with no clothing, no text, no letters, no numbers, one or two simple hand-drawn marker props only, no arrows, lots of empty white space, only red, black and white colors, whiteboard explainer animation look
style_lock.negative_prompt: color photo, photorealistic, 3d render, shading, gradients, text, letters, numbers, watermark, mouth, extra colors
reference_assets: MafiaOfBusiness/brand/host/host-reference-clean.jpeg -- clean whiteboard stickman on a plain white background, sent as the reference image with every scene request by scenes/flux_orchestrator.py.
style_lock.generation_notes: Converted to the RedHat Engineer look on 2026-09-30. FLUX.2 [klein] on Cloudflare Workers AI takes a reference image, which is what keeps the red-fedora stickman the same character beat to beat. It has no negative_prompt, cfg_scale or steps parameters: those two fields are kept only so the raphael and cloudflare-SDXL fallback backends still run, and neither keeps the host on-model. Known ceiling: more than 2 distinct characters in one shot collapses to 1 rendered subject -- write multi-character beats as shot/reverse-shot pairs. The earlier painterly Indian-mystery look is retired (see reports/changelog.md).
style_lock.generation_tooling: MafiaOfBusiness/scripts/scenes/flux_orchestrator.py (IMAGE_BACKEND=flux, the default) POSTs each beat to Workers AI with the reference image; 3 parallel workers, retry with backoff on 429/5xx, stops the batch on bad credentials or a spent daily quota.

audio.pacing_note: Gaps are looser than a Shorts channel's (0.25s/0.4s) -- a 5-7 minute documentary-paced episode doesn't need to stay maximally dense, unlike a 30-60s short.

ambience.note: No music. A few synthesized effects plus a soft whoosh on every scene cut, at a fixed low gain. Keyword cues are tuned to technology stories (forge, patent paper, lightning, water power). The cold-open bed and heartbeat/footstep/whisper cues are mystery-atmosphere effects and stay disabled for this channel unless an episode asks for them in 02_script/ambience_plan.json.

transitions.note: A soft whoosh peaks on every scene cut (beat 2 onward), variant + small gain jitter derived from the beat number. Never deduped by min_gap_seconds. Skipped on climax_reveal beats, which get reveal_sting. Disable per episode with 02_script/ambience_plan.json {"disable": ["transition"]}.

format.animation_stage_note: Every scene gets a Ken Burns push in/out via ffmpeg zoompan on the static generated image. Direction read from 05_scenes/shotlist.json's "motion" field, falling back to alternating in/out. 6-10s per scene: flat whiteboard art has less to look at than a painted scene, so it is cut faster.
format.no_intro_outro: No separate branded intro sting / outro card spliced in. The cold-open beat IS the first scene; the episode ends on the aftermath section's last beat. assemble_episode.py concatenates scene clips directly.

captions.engine_note: Word timing comes from edge-tts's own WordBoundary events, captured in generate_narration_chunks.py / remapped to absolute time in stitch_audio.py's word_timings.json -- no ASR/transcription step. Rendered as an ASS file, burned in via ffmpeg's libass-backed subtitles filter in assemble_episode.py.
captions.font_family_note: A locally-installed bold sans (no new dependency).
captions.highlight_color_note: A red accent (#E53935), in ASS's &H00BBGGRR byte order. Was violet (#8B5CF6) until 2026-09-29.
captions.alignment_note: ASS numpad alignment: 2 = bottom-center anchor. Actual vertical position is set by margin_v_ratio below.
captions.margin_v_note: Fraction of video height kept clear below the caption's baseline -- lower than Dmoo Way's 0.30 because a 16:9 horizontal video has no bottom-of-screen platform UI (like/comment/share cluster) to clear.
captions.max_gap_note: A phrase never spans a pause longer than this -- prevents captions from gluing the end of one sentence to the start of the next across stitch gaps.
captions.animation_style_note: Each phrase is one ASS line spanning its full on-screen time, re-emitted once per word so the highlighted word can move across otherwise-static text.

baselines.baselines_note: Average view duration and click-through rate are the primary signals: early analytics showed retention, not quality, was the weak point on the old explainer videos.
